content:
The EPFO is crediting 8.25% interest for FY 2025-26 to 34 crore member accounts, with most passbooks expected to show the credit by July 15, 2026. To verify yours is correct, pull up your passbook via the UMANG app, find the line "Int. Updated up to 31/03/2026," and compare the amount against a simple monthly calculation. If it looks off by more than rounding, epfigms.gov.in is your next step, but only after 90 days have passed.

This post covers how EPF interest works and how to verify it. It is general information, not personalised financial advice.

  • EPFO is processing 8.25% interest for FY 2025-26 across 34 crore accounts, with credits expected by July 15, 2026.
  • EPF interest is calculated monthly on your closing balance at 0.6875% per month, then credited as one entry after March 31.
  • The new CITES platform has cut the usual October-November credit timeline down to July, faster than any previous year.
  • Check via UMANG app (Services > EPFO > View Passbook) or member.epfindia.gov.in; look for "Int. Updated up to 31/03/2026."
  • If the amount seems wrong after 90 days, file on epfigms.gov.in with your UAN, PF number, and a passbook screenshot.

What's Happening With Your EPF Interest Right Now?

On July 8, Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya confirmed that EPFO is distributing over Rs 1.44 lakh crore in interest to 34 crore member accounts for FY 2025-26, at the same rate as last year: 8.25%. Field offices were directed to complete all credits by July 15.

That's a real shift. In most previous years, EPF interest didn't show up in passbooks until October or November. This kind of delay has occured even when the rate was set months earlier. The new Centralised IT Enabled Services (CITES) platform processes everything centrally, cutting months off the wait. So if you're checking your passbook this week and the interest line is still blank, give it until the 15th.

How Is Your EPF Interest Calculated for FY 2025-26?

Your EPF interest for FY 2025-26 is calculated monthly on your closing balance at 0.6875% per month (8.25% divided by 12). The amounts across all 12 months are totaled and credited once, after March 31. Only the EPF portion earns interest; the EPS component doesn't.

A concrete example. Say you had Rs 3,00,000 in EPF at the start of April 2025, and you and your employer together put in around Rs 3,000 a month toward EPF (not the EPS portion). By April's close your balance is roughly Rs 3,03,000, earning around Rs 2,083 in interest that month. By March 2026 the balance is around Rs 3,33,000, earning about Rs 2,290. Add all 12 months and you'd arrive somewhere around Rs 26,000 to Rs 27,000 in total interest for the year.

This is a rough estimate. The exact figure depends on when contributions clear each month, since EPFO calculates interest on the closing balance after all deposits land. For precision, download your full passbook and check month by month. That's the only way to catch a real discrepancy.

One thing many people miss: if your employer contributes 12% of your basic salary, only 3.67% goes to EPF. The remaining 8.33% goes to EPS, the pension fund. Your interest is calculated on the smaller EPF portion only, which is often less than people expect.

How Do You Check If Your EPF Interest Has Been Credited?

Open the UMANG app, go to Services, then EPFO, then View Passbook. Log in with your UAN and the OTP sent to your registered number, and look for the entry "Int. Updated up to 31/03/2026." That single line is your FY26 interest credit. You can also check via member.epfindia.gov.in or by texting EPFOHO UAN to 7738299899.

  1. UMANG app: Download it, go to Services, find EPFO, then View Passbook. Log in with UAN and OTP. The passbook lists entries month by month, with the interest showing as one annual credit line.
  2. EPFO member portal: Go to member.epfindia.gov.in, log in with UAN and password, click View Passbook. Same information as the app, slightly less phone-friendly.
  3. SMS: Text EPFOHO UAN to 7738299899 from your registered mobile. You'll recieve a quick balance summary, though it won't show the interest as a separate line item. For verification, use the passbook.

If the interest line isn't showing yet, the credit is still being processed in batches accross field offices. Give it until July 15.

What If the Amount Looks Wrong?

If your expected EPF interest differs significantly from what's credited, start by recalculating using your monthly closing balances. A gap of a few hundred rupees is normal rounding; EPFO truncates fractions during calculation. If the difference exceeds Rs 500 to Rs 1,000 and your KYC is complete, wait 90 days, then file a grievance on epfigms.gov.in.

Before filing, check one thing that's definately worth confirming: whether accounts from previous employers have been properly transferred. If you've changed jobs and never triggered an EPF transfer, interest from that old account may sit in a separate, unconsolidated account rather than show up in your current passbook. That looks like missing interest but isn't.

After 90 days, if the number still looks off:

  • Go to epfigms.gov.in
  • Select "PF Account" as the grievance type
  • Attach a screenshot of your passbook showing the discrepancy
  • Include your UAN, PF number, and a brief note on the difference you've calculated

You can also visit your regional EPFO office with Aadhaar and UAN. They can pull up the backend status and tell you whether it's a delay or something that needs correcting.

Frequently Asked Questions

Will I get EPF interest if I withdrew my full balance before March 31?

No. If your account was fully settled before FY26 ended, interest stops at the month of withdrawal. You won't receive the FY26 annual credit. EPFO calculates interest only on balances that remain in the account through March 31, 2026.

My passbook shows no interest for two years. Is that an error?

Possibly not. If you haven't contributed for three or more years, your account may be classified as inoperative and interest stops accruing. Contact your regional EPFO office with your UAN to check the account status. Active accounts always get credited annually.

Does the 8.25% interest apply to the EPS portion too?

No. The EPS component funds your pension and doesn't earn EPF interest. Only the EPF portion earns 8.25% per year. Many people overcount their expected interest because they apply the rate to the full 12% employer contribution, when only 3.67% of that goes to EPF.

How is interest calculated if I joined a company mid-year?

Interest starts from the month your first contribution is received. If you joined in November 2025, you'd get five months of interest for FY26 (November through March), not twelve. Your passbook will show interest only from the month contributions began, which is correct.

Is EPF interest taxable?

Generally no, up to a threshold. Interest on EPF contributions up to Rs 2.5 lakh per year is tax-free. If you contribute more through VPF on top of mandatory EPF, interest on the amount above Rs 2.5 lakh becomes taxable from FY 2021-22 onwards under the revised rules.

The Short Version

Your 8.25% EPF interest for FY 2025-26 is being credited now, with most accounts updating by July 15. Check your passbook via UMANG or the EPFO portal and look for "Int. Updated up to 31/03/2026." Small differences from your estimate are normal rounding. If the gap is significant after 90 days, file on epfigms.gov.in with your UAN and passbook screenshot. Most of what looks like a missing credit in July is a processing delay, not a mistake.
